name: A helping hand
text: {player} gave a hand at {place} and wouldn't take anything for it.
variants: They say {player} carried half of {place} up a hill and didn't once mention it after.
Somebody helped old Maud with her fence. {player}, it was. Odd, in a good way.

name: Open-handed
text: {player} gave a thing away at {place} without being asked twice.
variants: Open-handed, that one. My cousin says it's either goodness or guilt, and either way she'd take the gift.

name: A life spared
text: There was a blade at a throat near {place} and {player} put it away again.
variants: {player} let one go. Some call that soft. The one who was let go calls it something else.

name: A name put back
text: A name went back on the Wardens' roll, and it was {player} who carried it there.
variants: They wrote a name back in at the Rest. Ink and everything. {player}'s doing.

name: A hearth tended
text: A cold hearth at {place} is warm again. {player} wouldn't say who lit it, which is how we know.
variants: Somebody swept and laid a fire in an empty house at {place}. That's a small thing. Small things are the whole of it.

name: The long table
text: {player} paid for a long table at {place} and sat at the end of it like anyone.
variants: Ale for the whole room, and nobody's seen the bottom of the purse yet. {player}, they say.

name: A cure carried
text: The fever at {place} broke the day {player} walked in with a jar.
variants: {player} came back with the thing the apothecary said grows nowhere near here. It grows somewhere, evidently.

name: A child home
text: A child walked out of the dark at {place} holding {player}'s hand, and the whole street cried about it.
variants: They'd given the little one up. {player} hadn't.

name: The unburied buried
text: {player} put somebody in the ground near {place} who had been waiting a long while.
variants: No name for the stone, so {player} cut a bell into it instead. That'll do.

name: A debt settled
text: Somebody's debt at {place} got paid off by a stranger. {player}, if you believe the tallyman.
variants: The ledger's clean and nobody will say who cleaned it, which is the same as saying it.

name: Light fingers
text: Things go missing around {place} when {player} is about. Not accusing. Just counting.
variants: My aunt's good spoon walked off the same afternoon {player} did.
Lock your shutters at {place}. That's all I'll say, and I've said it.

name: A nosy stranger
text: {player} was in a room at {place} that wasn't {player}'s room to be in.
variants: Wandered right through like a cat that's decided it lives there.

name: Quick to strike
text: {player} raised a hand at {place}. In a settled place. In daylight.
variants: There's arguing and there's what {player} did, and they're not neighbours.

name: Blood at the door
text: There is blood on the stones at {place} and the word going round is {player}.
variants: Bar the door. I'm not saying it twice and I'm not saying the name again either.
They found them cold at {place}. Everybody knows. Nobody will write it down.

name: A price on safety
text: {player} put a price on somebody's quiet night at {place}.
variants: Pay or don't, they were told. That's not trade, that's weather with a face.

name: A name struck out
text: A name came off the roll and {player} held the pen.
variants: Struck through, twice, so it couldn't be read under. Somebody wanted that name gone properly.

name: A hearth put out
text: The fire at {place} is out and cold and it didn't go out on its own. {player} was seen.
variants: You don't put out a hearth. You just don't. Whatever they meant by it.

name: An opened grave
text: A barrow near {place} is open at the top and {player} came back heavier than they went in.
variants: The dead don't need rings, {player} says. The dead have opinions, {place} says.

name: A broken word
text: {player} gave a word at {place} and then didn't.
variants: Round here a promise is most of what a person is. Draw your own picture.

name: A named thing put down
text: The thing under {place} has a killer now, and the killer is {player}.
variants: It had a name. It doesn't need one any more. {player} saw to that.
Grown folk are singing about {player} in the taproom and they've got the tune wrong already.

name: A beast with a name
text: {player} killed the beast they'd been naming at {place} for two winters.
variants: We'd named it. That's how long it had been at us. {player} unnamed it.

name: A nest cleared
text: You can walk the track by {place} again. {player} went in and the nest is quiet.
variants: Cleared out, the lot of them. The children are allowed as far as the stile again.

name: The road is open
text: The camp that was pricing the road near {place} isn't pricing anything now. {player}.
variants: Carters are coming through again and bringing gossip with them, which is the real profit.

name: Something the basin needed
text: {player} did a thing at {place} that everyone from the Mere to the ash is going to be talking about.
variants: There's talk it matters to all of us and not just to {place}. Rare, that.

name: Work done
text: {player} did work for the people who keep {place}, and they're saying so out loud, which is not their habit.
variants: They don't thank people as a rule. They thanked {player}.

name: What was asked
text: {player} finished what was asked at {place}, which is rarer than heroics and worth more.
variants: Said they'd do it, then did it. Write it on a wall.

name: Off the board
text: Another notice off the board at {place}, and {player}'s name on the tally.
variants: Board's looking thin. Somebody's working.

name: Left undone
text: {player} started something at {place} and the something is still standing there, started.
variants: Half a job is a whole disappointment, my mother used to say, usually to me.

name: Came back out
text: {player} went down into the deep place at {place} and — this is the part — came back out.
variants: Down there a week, up in an afternoon, and wouldn't say a word about the middle of it.

name: A stone named
text: There's a Hearthstone at {place} with a name on it now, and {player} is the one who said it.
variants: Naming a stone. Grand old word for a small warm thing. It's already warmer up there.

name: A song going round
text: There's a verse about {player} going round {place} and two of the rhymes are frankly a stretch.
variants: The fiddler at {place} has a new one and it's about {player} and it's mostly lies, but good lies.

name: Good company
text: {player} made the room at {place} laugh, and a room that laughs stays warm a while after.
variants: Turns out {player} dances. Badly. Enormously badly. We liked it.

name: Bad manners
text: {player} was rude in the middle of {place}, in front of people who remember things.
variants: Gestures like that are for the road, not for a market. Somebody should tell them. Somebody will.

name: Paid up
text: {player} settled up with the law at {place} without much fuss, which counts for something round here.
variants: Paid the fine, took the look, went on. Fair enough.

name: A spell in a cell
text: {player} did a stretch in the cell at {place}. Not long. Long enough to be mentioned.
variants: Out again already. Either the cell's soft or somebody spoke for them.

name: Seen to fall
text: Somebody saw {player} go down near {place}. And then not stay down, which is the strange part.
variants: We all saw it. We're all being careful how we say it.

name: The Toll hums
text: The Toll's humming. Forty metres of cracked bronze in a hole in the ground and it's humming like a fly in a jug, and my grandfather said it did that once before and then wouldn't finish the sentence.
variants: The Cracked Toll is humming. My grandmother said it did that once before and then wouldn't say when.
Stand in the lip of it and your teeth go funny. That's new.

name: A village gone quiet
text: There was a hamlet out past {place}. Was. Ask a Warden and watch them go careful.
variants: I can't bring the name of it to mind, and that's exactly what they warn you about.

name: The Wardens are short-handed
text: The Wardens are short of hands at the Rest and taking on strangers, which tells you how short.
variants: They'll have anyone who can hold a lantern and read a name. Anyone at all. Think on that.

name: Something taken from the Roll
text: Something went missing out of the Roll room at Wardens' Rest and they are being extremely calm about it.
variants: A page. One page. You'd think it was the whole book the way Hesk is walking about.

name: Alone, and out again
text: They're saying {player} went into the Tumbled Watch alone and came out. Alone. I had it off a carter who had it off a Warden, so that's nearly first-hand.

name: Three loaves
text: You'll not have heard, because they'd not say it themselves: {player} carried bread to a door in {place} where nobody's carried anything in nine years. Three loaves. Three means something here.

name: Bar your door
text: Bar your door if {player}'s about. No, I'll not say what I heard. I'll say the dogs in {place} went quiet and they don't do that for nothing.

name: Up the Hushline Stair
text: That one came up the Hushline Stair. Walked up. Nobody walks up. A Warden named them at the top step and hasn't slept right since, they say.

name: Gosling has a verse about it
text: Merrick Gosling's got a verse about {player} now, and it's got to {place} already with two extra stanzas and a tune it was never written in.

name: Pennywort's wheel
text: Pennywort's wheel turns with no water in the race. He's grinding with it and selling the flour and the flour keeps a month, and I've bought it, and so have you.

name: The lane that isn't
text: There was a lane off the Tamwick road that went up to a place with a hare cut on the well. Went to turn up it last month out of habit and there's no lane. Hedged right over. I sat in the cart a while.

name: The Larkbourne Boys
text: The Boys are on the Larkbourne road again, keeping hall in the old Warden tower that's lying on its side. Nobody remembers the Larkbourne Boys, which is exactly what they're banking on.

name: The singing yew
text: Orchard men in {place} let the barrow-wights come up as far as the old yew and no further. Thing's got a bell grown into its heart and it hums, and a wight will stop dead at it and turn round. Nobody knows why and nobody's asking too loudly.

name: Bells on a still night
text: The buoy bells out on the Mere have been ringing on still nights. Still nights, mind. No swell. Four of us have heard it off {place} and we'd agreed not to make anything of it.

name: The hermit of Willow Isle
text: There's a hermit on Willow Isle who was a Tallymen clerk and stopped counting. He'll tell you the true price of anything you like, exactly, and then refuse to sell it to you.

name: The door with no hinges
text: There's a door under the city with no hinges that opens for names. Say your own if you're anybody. If you're nobody, say the name of whoever's wronged you; they say it finds that funny.

name: The Lamp is dimmer
text: The Lamp's dimmer than it was. The keeper won't say so to a Sayer, because a Sayer would come and measure it, and we've all seen what their measuring does to a thing that was working.

name: The Nave answers singing
text: The water in the Drowned Nave rises when there's singing in it. That's not a story; ask anyone from {place} who's rowed a Sayer out there and had to row them back faster.

name: Eelfathom runs late
text: The pool at Eelfathom runs a few seconds behind. You wave and it waves after. Lad from {place} sat there a whole afternoon trying to catch it up and came home very quiet.

name: The shaft at Oskeld
text: The shaft at Oskeld sings when the wind's right, and the clans say there's a thing walking in it that's bone and rock and was people once. Half the Hold says it isn't a person. The other half won't say either way in front of children.

name: The eighth verse
text: The Rope-Song's got seven verses and a hole where the eighth ought to be. Every memory-keeper for a thousand years has taken that breath and not one of them can tell you whose name goes in it.

name: The Briar going grey
text: The Briar's going grey in patches. Fourteen at midwinter, nineteen now, and the forester counts them every morning and has stopped telling people the number.

name: The fire that went out
text: Out on the heath there's a fire that went out a hundred and seventy years ago with Greyfold's people still sat round it passing a cup. They'll not rise unless you touch the cup. They wave, though. They all wave.

name: The thirteenth
text: The Choir's got twelve. There's a thirteenth lying face down a mile off as if it walked away, and it's got a head, and the head isn't the same as the others, and there's a Sayers' camp digging at it and arguing.

name: It opens for the known
text: The Order's been keeping that ring a hundred and seventy-seven years waiting on somebody the door'll open for. It opens for the known, they say. Which means every one of them who kept faith with it and died grey at the ring was never going to be enough.

name: The woman who cuts the numbers
text: There's a woman at the canal end of Lantern Row who cuts the numbers into the watch's crossbows. Every stock in this city has been through her hands, and she'll greet a sergeant by his number and then apologise for it. If you want one that isn't a crime to carry, hers is the only door.
variants: Lathe, at the canal end. She'll make you one under charter and she'll ask you three questions first, in the same order, and she has never once changed the order for anybody.
There's a register on a counter on Lantern Row with every crossbow in this city written into it. That book's kept more men out of a cell than the charter-board has.

name: The bone-bench
text: The Kharrow bone-bench won't work for anyone the Hand hasn't had. That's not a price and there's no arguing it: Ordda ko-Brindle will hear you right out, and then she'll ask whether you've lain a night in the palm, and that's the end of it either way.
variants: Third ledge, past the chain-drawers. The bone comes over on the cart from the crag and a Brindle comes with it, because you don't hand a giant to a stranger.
She weighs the bone before she cuts and after, and walks the difference back up the scree. An hour and a half each way. Half the year in the dark.

name: Blades that don't ring
text: Every knight at the Ash makes their own blade, and they come out black, and they don't ring. Ask one why and she'll say it's because ash is what grows there now, and she'll be telling you the truth and not the reason.
variants: They quench them in the fire-ash out of the chapter-house bell. A grey sword for grey country, they say, and they say it in the voice people use for a second meaning.

name: Hallam's one sword
text: Hallam Ashdown's hung that sword up. Nineteen year under the bed behind his wife's winter boots, and now it's on the hooks over the bellows where the whole street can see it, and he'll talk about it, which he never would. Half the lane's been in to look and bought a nail out of politeness.
variants: The red door's got a sword over the bellows. Ask him about it. Go on, ask him. You'll want to be sitting down.

name: The poppy picked
text: Somebody picked the red poppy out on the heath. The one. There's a ring of stones round a hole now, and the pilgrims walk out to look at the hole instead. {player}, they're saying.

name: The poppy watered
text: The cup by the red poppy was used again, and not by a pilgrim. {player} walked out across the grey to water one flower, and walked back. The Ash has been kind about it, which the Ash rarely is.

name: The heaps under the yew
text: Somebody's been at the yew in Foxglove Dell by night: splitting the berries, keeping the seed and leaving the red in little heaps under the tree. The red's the half that won't hurt you. Tansy Cresswell sat up four nights and saw nothing, and her cousin Nell has stopped guessing out loud.

name: Crossed Windgate
text: There's a Dreugh woman at Windgate takes three marks to let you cross a pass that's been shut ten winters. People pay it. Then they can say they crossed Windgate, and she's written it in the book, so it's true.
